title: Unified Monolithic Model across Different Bounded Contexts (False Cognates)
pattern: Forcing different business subdomains (Bounded Contexts) to use a single monolithic domain entity because they describe the same physical entity.
why_bad: It creates a "false cognate" model where different teams step on each other's code, database fields have weird contradictions, and the entity carries massive optional fields that are irrelevant to most operations.
detection: A single domain class/struct containing distinct clusters of fields that are only ever accessed together by separate, non-overlapping application services.
counterexample: Shared identity mapping (e.g., standard key structures) where only the primary identifier and basic authentication credentials are shared.
source: *Domain-Driven Design* (Evans), Chapter 14: "duplicate concepts and false cognates", p. 410.
